page: Amazon Web Services m7a.8xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with a dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs, operating at one thread per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

The AMD EPYC processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 foundation, AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), and AVX-512 Brain Floating Point 16-bit (BF16), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA extensions. In performance testing, the instance demonstrates strong CPU capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for both single-core and multi-core stress-ng benchmarks, as well as Passmark CPU tests covering encryption, physics, and extended instructions.

The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers strong read bandwidth for small cached blocks and strong write bandwidth for large uncached blocks, though large-block read bandwidth and Passmark memory scores fall in the average range. The instance excels in database operations, with strong performance in Passmark database tests and Redis SET operations, which exceed 67 million operations per second. For machine learning tasks, it achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds for small LLM models and strong text generation performance for both small and medium models.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the m7a.8xlarge is suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database management, and moderate machine learning inference. The lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider for I/O-heavy applications.
